title: Records Management and Retention Policy
summary: How we create, correct, store, keep and securely destroy every record we hold about the people we support, our staff and the running of the service, in CareFlow, on paper and in people's homes. Contains our full retention schedule and the rules for holds, archiving, destruction, branch closure and transfer of the business. For all staff.

keyPoints.intro: Every record you write may later be read by the next care worker, a GP, a family, a coroner or the person themselves. This policy tells you how to write and correct records, what paper you may use and why nothing is ever deleted early.
points: Record care in CareFlow on your work phone, under your own log-in, before you check out. Phone anything urgent to the office or On-call Manager before leaving; add anything else as a late entry before your shift ends, or phone it through afterwards.
Write facts: what you saw, heard, did and were told, and who told you. Label any opinion as your opinion and give the reason. Use respectful, plain words and the person's preferred name.
Never delete, overwrite or backdate an entry. Correct a mistake by adding a dated correcting entry that says what was wrong and why. Altering or hiding a record is a disciplinary matter.

Take body map photographs or video only as the Consent to Care Policy allows, and voice notes only of your own account, in the CareFlow app on your work phone. Never keep personal notes, photographs, recordings or copies of records on any phone.
The only paper you use is the paper another of our policies names, such as a back-up MAR sheet. Never keep notes or copies of records anywhere else.

Keep paper out of sight while travelling and never leave it in an unattended vehicle. Bring any you collect to the branch office by the end of your shift, in a sealed envelope through the letterbox if it is closed. Never bin it.
Keep the home copy of the care plan and other papers in the place the person chooses. Tell the office the same day if any are missing, because that may be a data breach.
If you hear of a complaint, claim, solicitor's letter, police inquiry, inquest or investigation, tell the office the same working day so that the records can be protected from destruction.

Records are kept for the periods in our retention schedule, then destroyed securely by managers with approval. Nobody destroys or deletes a record because care has ended, someone has died or a complaint has been made.

When a person's care ends, the Field Care Supervisor collects our papers from the home within 5 working days. Documents that belong to the person, such as their letters and prescriptions, stay with them.
On or before your last working day, return every paper record you hold. Your CareFlow access ends that day.
Complete information governance training, which includes record keeping, in your first week and every 12 months.

blocks.p: {{organisation}} keeps records because people's safety depends on them. A care worker arriving alone at 7am relies on what the last care worker wrote; a GP, family, coroner or the person may later need to know what care was given and why. The law requires us to keep securely an accurate, complete and contemporaneous record of the care given and decisions taken for each person we support, and the records needed about our staff and the running of the service (Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, regulation 17(2)(c) and (d)). Data protection law requires us to keep personal information secure and for no longer than we need it (UK GDPR, Article 5).
Nothing is destroyed early or while it may be needed for a complaint, claim, enquiry or investigation; nothing is kept without a reason; and no record is ever altered to hide what happened.

This policy makes sure every record is accurate, written at the time, attributable and held in CareFlow; kept for a set period and protected while needed; destroyed securely with evidence; and kept safe when care ends, a branch closes, the business transfers or we change systems.

This policy applies to every record we create or receive, in any format: CareFlow entries, photographs, video and audio recordings, scanned documents, emails and paper. It applies to the Directors and every employee, and through their agreements to agency workers, students, contractors and suppliers.

Owned elsewhere: daily visit note content (Daily Records and Visit Notes Procedure); eMAR recording (Medicines Administration Records (MAR and eMAR) Procedure); lawful bases (Data Protection Policy); sharing (Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy); people's own requests (Subject Access and Individual Rights Procedure); breaches (Personal Data Breach Procedure); technical security and backups (Information and Cyber Security Policy); staff record content and access (Staff Personal Data and HR Records Policy); and policies (Policy Management and Document Control Policy).

rows: Care record

Everything we hold about one person we support: initial assessment with any recording and transcript, care plan and every previous version, risk assessments, daily visit notes, including voice notes, eMAR, body maps with any photographs and video, check-in/check-out records, including location, money records, consent and capacity records, correspondence, the service agreement and the person's documents scanned into CareFlow.
Care ends
The date of the last visit when a package ends for good, including when the person dies. A suspension, such as a hospital admission, is not an end of care.
Closed record
A care record after care ends, a staff record after employment ends, or a governance record after the matter it concerns is closed or the version is replaced.
Retention hold
A recorded instruction that named records must not be destroyed, whatever their retention period, while they may be needed for a complaint, claim, investigation or inquiry.
Information asset owner
The manager accountable for a group of records, as set out under Roles and responsibilities: the Registered Manager, the HR Manager or the Nominated Individual.

blocks.p: The Directors are accountable for our records. They approve this policy and its retention schedule and decide the records arrangements before any branch closure, transfer of the business or closure of {{organisation}}.

As Senior Information Risk Owner, the Nominated Individual is the information asset owner for governance records. They decide extensions, lift holds and approve any early destruction, on the Data Protection Officer's advice where personal data is involved; sign off the destruction log each quarter; contract and check our destruction and storage providers; and keep the retention periods in the record of processing activities in line with this schedule.

The Registered Manager owns this policy and is the information asset owner for care and branch records: they place holds on and approve the destruction of those records and check closed care records. The Deputy Manager covers these duties in their absence.

The Deputy Manager prepares the quarterly retention review of care, branch and governance records, checks scanning and closed records, and carries out the records and data protection audit each December. The HR Manager, as information asset owner for staff, applicant and Director records, prepares and approves their quarterly review, places holds for tribunals and staff claims, and creates each staff record summary.

subsections.heading: Care Coordinators and Field Care Supervisors

blocks.p: Care Coordinators close the care record when care ends, correct care plan errors and save emails that form part of a record into CareFlow. Field Care Supervisors keep the home copy of the care plan current, collect our papers when care ends and check record keeping at every spot check.

Office staff scan and destroy paper, look after the confidential waste console and log retrieval of archived paper. On-call Managers record out-of-hours calls and decisions and keep the downtime log as set out below.

Everyone who works for us follows the standards below, uses paper only where this policy allows and tells the office the same working day about anything that may need a retention hold. Deliberately altering, hiding or destroying a record is handled under the Disciplinary Policy and Procedure.

bullets: Own log-in: every entry is made under the author's own CareFlow log-in, which records their name, the date and the time. Nobody uses or shares another person's log-in.

At the time: care is recorded during the visit and before check-out, otherwise as a late entry (below), with anything that cannot wait phoned to the office (the On-call Manager out of hours) before leaving the home. Office staff record calls and advice the same working day; On-call Managers record before the 10am handover; managers record each decision, with its reasons, when they make it.
Factual: what the author saw, heard, did and was told, and who told them, with the person's own words quoted where they matter. An opinion is labelled as the author's opinion, with the reason.
Complete: every planned task is recorded as done, declined or not done, with the reason, and any change noticed is recorded with who was told.

Respectful and clear: plain English and the person's preferred name; behaviour described rather than labelled, for example 'shouted and pushed my hand away' rather than 'aggressive'; no abbreviations except those the Daily Records and Visit Notes Procedure allows.

In the right place: information about other people is recorded only where it affects the person's care or risk; safeguarding detail goes only in the safeguarding record, with the daily visit notes saying only that a concern was reported; complaints go in the complaint record, not the care record; key safe codes go only in CareFlow's key safe code field and the encrypted business continuity access file.
On paper, where paper is allowed: black ink, the date and time, the person's name and date of birth on each page, and the author's printed name and signature.

subsections.heading: Correcting a record and late entries

blocks.p: Nobody deletes, overwrites or backdates an entry. A mistake is corrected by a new, dated entry that states what was wrong, the correct information and the reason, leaving the original visible. The author corrects their own entry; if they have left or cannot be reached, the Care Coordinator or manager who found the error does so and says so.

rows: Allergies, medicines, key safe information or resuscitation decisions
The same working day, with the care team told
Any other error affecting safety
Before the person's next visit
Other errors in a care record
Within 7 days
Gaps or errors in a staff record
Within 10 working days

blocks.p: An entry made after the event is marked as a late entry, with the time of the event and the reason it is late, and is made as soon as possible and always before the end of the author's shift. Anything remembered after the shift has ended is phoned to the office, or the On-call Manager out of hours, and recorded on the author's behalf, as the Daily Records and Visit Notes Procedure sets out. An entry made in the wrong person's record is the only entry that may be removed: the Registered Manager or Deputy Manager removes it the same working day, the author records it in the correct record as a late entry, a note in the wrong record records the removal with the incident log reference, and the error is handled under the Personal Data Breach Procedure.

CareFlow is our record system for care records as defined above; staff records in the staff record, training and compliance records, supervision and appraisal records and policy acknowledgements; and events in the incident log and safeguarding records. Records of running the service are kept outside CareFlow, in the governance records and the branch health and safety file. No record is kept on a personal phone, personal email, memory stick, personal cloud storage, messaging app or notebook. Body map photographs and video (Consent to Care Policy), voice notes giving the author's own account (Daily Records and Visit Notes Procedure) and initial assessment recordings and transcripts are made only in the CareFlow app on a work device and kept only in CareFlow, never on the device.

Paper is used only for: the papers kept in people's homes listed in the next section; the downtime log kept by Office staff and On-call Managers while CareFlow is unavailable (an On-call Manager working from home keeps it locked away and brings it to the branch office the next working day), scanned and shredded once every entry is transferred (Daily Records and Visit Notes Procedure); the key register in the branch office (Key Holding, Key Safes and Access to People's Homes Procedure); and original contracts signed as deeds. Any other paper we receive, such as letters, forms and signed documents, is scanned and destroyed as follows.

steps: Care workers keep paper records out of sight while travelling, never leave them in an unattended vehicle, and bring them to the branch office by the end of their shift, in a sealed envelope through the office letterbox if it is closed. Post and paper handed in are date-stamped on the day they arrive.
Within 2 working days of arrival, Office staff (the HR Manager for staff and applicant documents) scan the paper into the correct CareFlow record, naming the document type and date.
The person scanning checks every page against the paper: all pages present, readable and in the right person's record. A failed check is rescanned the same day.

Once the check is passed, the paper is shredded or placed in the locked confidential waste console the same day, unless it is a document listed above or it belongs to the person; documents belonging to the person are returned to them by hand or recorded delivery within 5 working days.

blocks.p: Email is not a record store. Managers, Care Coordinators, Field Care Supervisors and Office staff save any email, with attachments, that forms part of a person's care, an employee's employment or a decision about the service into the right CareFlow record within 1 working day. Our IT support provider deletes mailbox items automatically 2 years after they were sent or received, and deletes a leaver's mailbox 3 months after their last working day, once their line manager has saved anything that forms part of a record; mailboxes under a retention hold are excluded.

The person's home is not our premises, so we keep as little paper there as their care allows. Papers are kept where the person chooses, and the person and anyone they allow may read them. Care workers put them back after each visit and phone the office the same day if any are missing, so that the Registered Manager can decide whether it is a personal data breach. Notes that district nurses or other agencies keep in the home are theirs; we never remove or copy them.

blocks.p: Papers in the home never contain key safe codes, infection or blood-borne virus status, other people's risks, safeguarding information or staff contact details. Field Care Supervisors check at every spot check that the papers are current and that nothing else of ours is in the home. During a hospital admission the papers stay in the home, except the end of life summary, which goes with the person as the End of Life Care Policy sets out.

When care ends, the Field Care Supervisor collects our papers within 5 working days of the last visit, at the same visit as any final money count or return of keys. The person or their representative may keep their copy of the care plan, and we record that they did; documents that belong to the person, such as letters and prescriptions, stay with them. After a death, papers are collected with the agreement of the executor, administrator or next of kin, and never while the police or coroner have asked for the home to be left untouched. Where collection is delayed, the Care Coordinator records why and the date agreed; where papers cannot be recovered, the Registered Manager decides whether it is a personal data breach.

The periods below are our policy, never shorter than any legal minimum and based on the Digital Care Hub's records management code of practice for adult social care providers, which is sector guidance, not law. For every row:

bullets: Employment plus 6 years means 6 years from the last day of employment.

Where a record fits more than one row, or a commissioner's contract sets a longer period, the longest period applies. A care record linked to a serious incident, safeguarding record, complaint or claim is kept for as long as that linked record, if that is longer.
If a person returns to our care, or an employee rejoins, while their earlier record is still kept, the records are linked and the period runs from the end of the new episode.

A retention hold overrides every period. A record type not listed here is kept for the period its owning policy or procedure sets or, where none does, until the Nominated Individual sets one within 1 month of the owner asking; either is added at the next review of this policy.

blocks.p: The HR Manager creates the summary before destroying the full staff record; the 75th birthday follows the Digital Care Hub schedule. Legal minimums: working time records 2 years; PAYE records 3 years after the tax year; minimum wage and holiday records 6 years; automatic enrolment records 6 years from when each must first be kept (opt-out notices 4 years).

blocks.p: A record is never destroyed while it is, or may be, needed for a complaint, claim, solicitor's letter, tribunal, inquest, safeguarding enquiry or Safeguarding Adults Review, police investigation, investigation or enforcement by CQC, HSE or the Information Commission, open rights request or public inquiry. Anyone who learns of one tells the office the same working day.

steps: The information asset owner (the Nominated Individual where more than one owner is involved) places the hold the same working day in the retention hold register in the governance records: the records covered, by CareFlow reference number, the reason, the date and a review date.

The owner tells the manager who prepares the destruction list for those records (Deputy Manager or HR Manager) and, for mailboxes or alarm recordings, our IT support provider or lone worker device supplier the same working day, so that the records are left off every destruction list and excluded from automatic deletion.
The owner reviews each hold at least every 6 months and records the review.
Only the Nominated Individual lifts a hold, when the matter and any appeal have ended. The records then return to their normal period and, if it has passed, go on the next quarterly destruction list.

blocks.p: Records created specifically in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, such as outbreak, testing, PPE supply and staff vaccination decision records, are under a standing hold until the UK Covid-19 Inquiry has ended or has confirmed which records it needs, as the Digital Care Hub code advises.

An information asset owner may apply to the Nominated Individual, with the reason, to keep records beyond their period, for example because a claim is likely. The Nominated Individual decides within 1 month on the Data Protection Officer's advice, and the records are kept while the decision is made. An approved extension is entered in the retention hold register with a review date no more than 2 years ahead, and never runs beyond 20 years from the last entry unless the law or this schedule sets longer.

When care ends, the Care Coordinator records the end date and reason in the care plan within 1 working day of the last visit and ends the person's future visits and allocations, so that care workers no longer see the record. Within 10 working days of the last visit, the Registered Manager or Deputy Manager checks that the record is complete: final daily visit notes, the eMAR closed with a note of what happened to the medicines, the final money reconciliation scanned, keys returned, the key safe code removed and our papers collected. They record in a closing note in the care plan which retention rule applies and the destruction date. When employment ends, the staff record is closed under the Staff Personal Data and HR Records Policy and the leaver returns any paper record they hold, and their CareFlow access ends, on their last working day.

Closed records stay in CareFlow, which is our archive; no separate copy is made. A closed record is opened only for a complaint, request, claim, investigation, enquiry, audit, invoice, reference or a returning person or employee. Anyone who opens a record more than 3 months after it was closed records the reason in the records access log in the governance records the same day.

Paper records from before we used CareFlow are kept in numbered, sealed archive boxes in a locked store in the branch office, or with an off-site storage company whose contract sets retrieval within 2 working days. The archive index in the governance records lists each box's record types, CareFlow reference numbers or names and dates of birth, date range and destruction date (the latest of its contents). Only the Registered Manager, Deputy Manager, HR Manager, Nominated Individual and Office staff named by the Registered Manager may open the index or a box. Every removal and return is logged in the index; nothing from the archive leaves the branch office, and an item removed is returned within 10 working days.
No record is destroyed automatically or without approval. Destruction follows a quarterly review:

steps: By the end of the first month of each quarter, the Deputy Manager (care, branch and governance records) and the HR Manager (staff, applicant and Director records) list the records whose retention period ended in the previous quarter, from the closing dates in CareFlow and the archive index.

For each record they check the retention hold register; open complaints, incidents, safeguarding records, rights requests and claims; any later episode of care or employment; any linked record kept longer; and any reason to apply for an extension.
Within 10 working days the information asset owner approves the list, removing anything that must be kept.

Before destruction, the Nominated Individual checks 5 items from each list (all if fewer) against the schedule and the register. A wrong item stops that list until the preparer has rechecked it in full.
Within 1 month of approval, the records are destroyed by the methods below.

The preparer completes the destruction log for each record, without names: record type, CareFlow reference or archive box number, date range, rule applied, approver, date and method of destruction and any certificate reference. The Nominated Individual signs off the quarter's log.

bullets: Deleting in CareFlow only hides a record, so CareFlow records are permanently deleted by the CareFlow supplier on the Nominated Individual's written instruction and confirms the deletion in writing. Deleted information is never restored from backups, which expire under the supplier's contract.

Paper is cross-cut shredded in the branch office to security level P-4 (DIN 66399) or higher, or placed in the locked confidential waste console, emptied by a contractor certified to BS EN 15713 that gives a certificate of destruction for each collection. Paper with personal information never goes in any household, office or public bin.
Off-site archive boxes are destroyed by the storage company, which gives a certificate listing each box.
Work phones, computers and storage media are wiped or physically destroyed by our IT support provider under the Information and Cyber Security Policy, with a certificate kept in the destruction log.
Destruction contractors and storage companies are entered in the register of processors before they receive any record, and the Nominated Individual checks their certification every year.

blocks.p: A record is destroyed before its period ends only with the Nominated Individual's approval on the Data Protection Officer's advice, for example where the law requires us to erase it; the destruction is entered in the destruction log with the reason. Once a record is destroyed, anyone asking for it is told the date and the rule under which it was destroyed.

sections.heading: Branch closure, transfer of the business and closure of the organisation

bullets: Branch closure: no record is destroyed because a branch closes (Statement of Purpose and Registration Procedure). Before the office closes, the Nominated Individual changes the branch on each person's and staff member's CareFlow record to another branch, whose Registered Manager becomes their information asset owner and is given CareFlow access to the closed branch's other records, and moves the key register and any archive boxes to that office or to off-site storage, updating the archive index.
A person moving to another provider: the new provider receives only what the Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy allows; the full care record stays with us for its retention period.

Transfer of the business to another legal entity: on legal and Data Protection Officer advice, the transfer agreement sets out which records move. Records of people whose care transfers and of employees who transfer move to the new provider on the transfer date, and those people are told in writing at least 2 weeks before. Closed records stay with {{organisation}} or pass to the new provider under a written agreement to keep them for the remaining periods in this schedule and answer requests for them.

Leaving CareFlow: before the contract ends, the Nominated Individual obtains from the CareFlow supplier an export of every record with its audit trail, checks within 1 month that the export is complete and readable, and only then instructs the supplier in writing to delete our data and confirm the deletion.

Closure of {{organisation}}: before the last visit, the Directors approve a records closure plan from the Nominated Individual, and every record is exported as above. On legal and Data Protection Officer advice the Directors either keep {{organisation}} in existence, paying the data protection charge, until the last retention period ends, or transfer the records under a written agreement to a successor that accepts this schedule. A named Director remains the contact for requests, and CQC, commissioners and the Information Commission are told where the records are held.

blocks.p: Shortfalls go into the service improvement plan within 5 working days. A record destroyed in error or while under a hold is recorded in the incident log and, where personal data is lost, handled under the Personal Data Breach Procedure.

The Registered Manager reviews this policy every 12 months, and sooner after a change in law or guidance, a serious incident, a breach involving records, an inspection or audit finding, or when monitoring shows the arrangements are not working. A retention period changed in this policy is changed in every one of our policies and procedures that states it in the same approval round. The Directors approve the policy under the Policy Management and Document Control Policy.
